review.verdict: A clean, legible split-scene that casts humans correctly and contrasts the falling-stock/lawsuit side against the triumphant rulebook side, but a safe-area clipping bug on the lawmaker's arm and a composition that echoes several recent building+falling-chart pieces hold it back from a strong pass.
revisionNotes: Pull the lawmaker's pointing arm/book back inside the safe margin — lint flags it breaching the safe area (x 739…1062, y 416…842); shift the lawmaker anchor left to ~x:0.74 or reduce scale to ~0.9 so the hand/book aren't flush against the right edge.

Change the lawmaker's pose from 'point' to a raised-overhead book pose so the rulebook reads as being lifted up triumphantly, matching the brief's 'raising the rulebook' metaphor instead of pointing off-canvas.

Rebalance composition: the top third of the frame is empty on both sides; raise the AI RULES tag and the chart/building group slightly to use the square better instead of clustering everything in the lower half.
Bump the briefcase prop's scale (currently ~1, tucked tight against the divider) to ~1.3 and nudge its offset so it reads clearly as a briefcase instead of a stray mark.

Composition echoes recent pieces that pair a building, falling chart and a human beside it (e.g. the 'Stock Falls / Jobs Cut' slopper); vary the chart's shape or building silhouette, or move the divider off-center, to differentiate.
Stagger the papers' rectangles at slightly different angles so the stack unmistakably reads as loose lawsuit papers rather than a plain filing box.
